title: Saudi Arabia: Kenyan domestic workers in forced-labour conditions (Amnesty investigation)
summary: Amnesty International's May 2025 report "Locked in, left out" is based on interviews with more than 70 Kenyan women who worked in Saudi homes and describes conditions that often amount to forced labour: about SAR 900 (US$240) a month for days of 16 hours or more, no days off for up to two years, passports and phones confiscated, and wages delayed or withheld. Women said recruitment agents in Kenya misrepresented the job; one was promised eight-hour days, a weekly day off and overtime, and worked from 6am to midnight with no day off in two years. Amnesty estimates about 150,000 Kenyans among roughly four million domestic workers in Saudi Arabia. This is an NGO investigation: no charges, sanctions or fines are recorded.

journey.note: Agents promised no fees, fair hours and rest days, and rushed contract signing.
